   AMES — We’ve all seen the imaginative touchdown celebrations. The joyful dances that Iowa State’s multi-talented tailback Aiden Flora performs multiple times seemingly on a weekly basis. Oh, and last week’s improvised Heisman Trophy-esque pose. 
  But what’s it like to block for him? To set that edge knowing the former walk-on from Adel could fly around it and sprint toward another six-point horizon? 
  Let Cyclone guard Austin Barrett explain.
  “Sometimes I’ll have my head buried in a block and I’ll hear the crowd go nuts and I’m like, ‘He obviously did something insane,’” said Barrett, who hopes to keep creating chasm-like creases for Flora and others when ISU (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) faces UCF (5-5, 3-4) at 5 p.m. Friday (FS1) at the Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando. “So it used to surprise me and now it doesn’t.”
  Flora’s ascension to the top of the FBS rushing charts with 1,335 yards no longer surprises anyone either, as fans and foes alike marvel at his ability to impact the game both as a runner, a punt returner, and, occasionally, a gadget play quarterback. The 6-0, 195-pound third-year talent is the only player in the country with 10-plus rushing touchdowns, two passing touchdowns and a punt return for touchdown this season — and slowing him down him is job one for every opponent the Cyclones have faced.
  “We’ve gotta try to handle (Flora) and (ISU) quarterback ( Jaylen Raynor ) and everything they do,” Knights head coach Scott Frost told reporters this week. “It’s gonna be a fun challenge for us. I know the guys are gonna come ready to go and we’ve gotta get ready for a good game.
  Las Vegas oddsmakers concur, as they currently peg UCF as a 1.5-point favorite. So a Bounce House “bounce” essentially put this matchup into pick ‘em territory, which makes X-factors such as Flora extra important because a big play or two within Friday’s tense 60-minute (or more) time frame could prove to be decisive.
  “We’re not gonna give up,” Flora said after rushing for 221 yards and three touchdowns in last week’s rout of Cincinnati. “Keep fighting. Keep pushing. Keep finishing. Strive to strain. Try to be the most physical team in the nation and just do your one-eleventh. Sometimes in (our) losses, we haven’t done our one-eleventh and when we do do that, we’re a good team.”
  Getting good gains on Friday could prove to be difficult for Flora and everyone else, as heavy rains are expected to continue to pelt central Florida right up until game time. And the Knights’ run defense has been solid, ranking eighth in the Big 12 in rushing yards allowed per game at 135.3 and first in the league in rushing touchdowns yielded (6). So while UCF’s front seven isn’t as daunting as those fielded by previous foes such as No. 2 Utah, No. 12 BYU, and No. 19 Arizona, it can be difficult to pierce with big plays, which are Flora’s speciality.
  “This is gonna be a tough task,” ISU head coach Jimmy Rogers said. “They’re a good football team.”
  And the Cyclones haven’t played their best football on the road. They’re 0-4 away from Jack Trice Stadium and Flora’s struggled to produce big plays in three of those four losses. But give him any daylight and he’s gone, whether at home or on the road — and let offensive tackle Jake Taylor to explain that dynamic.
  “Man, it’s so fun,” said Taylor, who like Flora was tabbed top be a team captain by his peers. “I’m doing the most I can, but when I don’t necessarily execute to the fullest ability and I just get in the way and he’s still having the explosive play, it’s unbelievable.”
  So is Flora’s speed, which is why the 6-6, 310-pound Taylor doesn’t always travel deep downfield to join in his eclectic celebrations.
  “I must say, as a bigger guy, (when) I see a 70-yard touchdown, I’m like, ‘Ah, I don’t know if I’m chasing that down,’” Taylor said. “I’ll celebrate with my other offensive lineman as we’re kind of waddling down the field, but I love him. He’s one of the greatest role models (and) one of the greatest leaders on our team.”
 Rob Gray Rob, an Ames native, joined Cyclone Fanatic in August, 2014 after nearly a decade and a half of working at Iowa's two largest newspapers. 
He spent 10 years at the Des Moines Register and, after a brief stint in public relations, joined the Cedar Rapids Gazette as an Iowa State correspondent three years ago. Rob specializes in feature stories for CF.
